transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess folks got worried after the fair. I was giving a talk there, and I got up on one of the tractors to, um, demonstrate something I thought was important — a “new pattern,” I called it. I was moving the controls around, probably more than I should’ve, and people were yelling for me to stop.

I don’t mean I was trying to scare anyone. I just… couldn’t seem to make myself quit right then. So they thought I ought to come in and talk to somebody. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you used amphetamines or methamphetamine recently?
No, sir, I don’t believe so. I mean, not anything like that. I try to stay away from that kind of thing. Is that… is that what people were thinking?
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Well… I don’t want to make too much of it, but yes, sometimes. Mostly out by the north pasture, near dusk. I’ll hear voices pretty clear, like they’re coming through the irrigation lines, telling me which rows are poisoned or blessed.

I know that sounds strange. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. It’s just… it happens even on weeks when I’m not all worked up or full of energy. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or on top of the world?

Yes… I suppose there have been mornings like that. Not all the time, but some mornings I wake up and it feels like the whole valley’s opening up just for me, like everything’s clear and I’m grinning at nothing.

I don’t mean to say I’m being foolish or anything. It feels good at first. But then if one of the hired hands questions what I’m doing, or my wife tells me to slow down, I can… well, I can snap pretty quick, like they’ve insulted the family name. I’m not proud of that. Does that answer it right?
Do you hear those voices even when you are not feeling especially high or full of energy?

Yes… yes, I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but there were some quieter weeks where I wasn’t feeling especially big or full of energy or anything like that.

And even then, I’d still hear the lines talking sometimes… and I’d still get the sense that the farm data had hidden warnings in it. Not all wild and worked up, just… still there. Is that what you mean?
Have the voices and hidden-warning beliefs been present for longer than one month?

Yes… more than a month, yes. I probably should’ve said that clearer.

It’s been going on, off and on, for about eleven months now — the voices and those… hidden warnings I think I’m seeing. I don’t mean every minute of every day, but it’s been around that long. Is that the sort of timeframe you needed?
Have you had a period lasting at least a week when you felt unusually high or irritable most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… I think there have been stretches like that, at least close to it. Some mornings I’d wake up feeling like the whole valley was opening up for me, and I’d be grinning at nothing, like everything was going my way.

I don’t like saying I was irritable, but… if a hired hand questioned me, or my wife told me to slow down, I could snap pretty quick, like they’d insulted the family name. It wasn’t my best self. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
During those high or irritable stretches, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel full of energy?

Yes… I suppose I did. I mean, I’d tell myself I was just resting my eyes, but most nights I’d only get maybe two or three hours in the chair… sometimes I don’t think I slept at all.

And then I’d still be up before the sun, feeling charged up, ready to work the place like nothing had happened. It didn’t feel bad at the time, if that makes sense… more like I was just finally keeping up. Is that what you mean by needing less sleep?
Was there ever a time when the voices or hidden warnings were happening for at least two weeks while your mood was otherwise normal—not especially high, irritable, or depressed?

Yes… yes, I think so.

There were a few quieter weeks where I wasn’t feeling all fired up or grand about things, and I wasn’t especially low either. Just… more like myself, I guess. But even then, I could still hear the lines talking, and I still felt like the farm data was carrying warnings in it.

I didn’t make as much of a fuss about it then, because I figured I was handling it better, but it was still there. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t know that I’d call it depressed for two whole weeks, Doctor. I’ve had rough spells, sure… everybody does, especially when things pile up. But most of the day, nearly every day, for that long? I’m not sure.

Maybe there were times I was quieter or more worn down than usual, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was. Is there a certain kind of “depressed” you mean?
Have you ever had a time when, for at least two weeks, you felt down or empty most of the day nearly every day?

I’m… I’m not sure I can say that, no.

I’ve had days where I felt kind of hollow or worn out, sure, but for two weeks straight, most of the day nearly every day… I don’t know that I’ve noticed it like that. I don’t want to overstate it just to give the “right” answer.

Maybe I’m not thinking about it the way you mean, though.
Over the whole time these problems have been going on, have the times when your mood was high or irritable made up most of it?

Yes… I suppose if I’m being honest, a lot of it has been that way.

I don’t want to make myself sound out of control or anything, but for most of this stretch I’ve been kind of… charged up, driven, like I had to keep pushing and making big plans. And I know I got irritable too, especially when people tried to slow me down or question me.

So… yes, I think those high or edgy times probably have made up most of it. Is that what you’re asking?
During those high or irritable periods, did your behavior ever get severe enough that you had to be hospitalized?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean… I don’t think I’d say it got to the point where I had to be hospitalized, at least not that I’m remembering that way.

There were times people were worried about me, sure, but being put in the hospital for it… I don’t know. I don’t want to say no if I’m misunderstanding what counts, but I can’t really point to that.
During one of those high or irritable periods, were you ever admitted to a hospital because of it?

I don’t think so… not admitted, no.

I mean, people may have been concerned, and I know I wasn’t always easy to deal with, but actually going into the hospital because of being high or irritable—I can’t say that happened. If there’s a specific kind of admission you mean, I might need you to explain it, but as far as I know, no.
During one of those high or irritable periods, did it cause serious problems in your life or work?

Yes… I guess it did. I don’t like saying it that way, because I’ve always handled the farm and I don’t want to sound incapable.

But my wife and the workers have had to step in more—making decisions I used to make about lenders, equipment, day-to-day operations. They’ve said it just doesn’t feel safe leaving me fully in charge when I’m like that.

And after what happened at the fair, people really started questioning whether I could keep running the farm at all. So… yes, I suppose it caused serious problems.
When the voices are happening during those quieter times, are you otherwise feeling emotionally about your usual self?

Mostly, yes… I mean, I wasn’t all worked up or feeling especially big or energized during some of those times.

There were a few quieter weeks where I felt more like myself emotionally, at least as far as I could tell. But I still heard the lines talking, and I still thought the farm data had hidden warnings in it. I know that may sound odd… I’m just trying to answer it plainly.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything you usually enjoy?

I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. I mean, I’ve had times where I didn’t feel like doing much, sure, but “almost everything” for two weeks… I don’t know.

I still usually find some satisfaction in the farm or family things, even if it’s not the same. So I don’t want to give you the wrong answer—maybe not that I can clearly say.
Before these past eleven months, had you ever heard the voices or noticed those hidden warnings at a time when you were not feeling high or irritable?

No… not that I can remember before this past year. The voices and those coded warnings, that all seems to have started around eleven months ago.

I might be missing something, but before then I don’t think I was noticing anything like that.
Was there ever a full month when you were hearing the voices or noticing the hidden warnings while not feeling especially high or irritable?

I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to overstate it, but there were several quieter weeks where I wasn’t feeling especially energized or grand or anything like that.

Even then, I was still hearing the lines talking, and I still believed the farm data had hidden warnings in it. So… if that counts as a full month, then yes, I think that did happen.

Yes… I guess it did. I don’t like saying it that way, because I’ve always handled the farm and I don’t want to sound incapable.

But my wife and the workers have had to step in more—making decisions I used to make about lenders, equipment, day-to-day operations. They’ve said it just doesn’t feel safe leaving me fully in charge when I’m like that.

And after what happened at the fair, people really started questioning whether I could keep running the farm at all. So… yes, I suppose it caused serious problems.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been any psychotic symptoms outside mood episodes beyond what is already reported, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: When the voices are happening during those quieter times, are you otherwise feeling emotionally about your usual self?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There were several quieter weeks when I was not especially energized or grand, but I still heard the lines talking and still believed the farm data was carrying hidden warnings.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the voices occur during quieter periods when mood is otherwise normal, which directly assesses psychotic symptoms occurring without a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Mostly, yes… I mean, I wasn’t all worked up or feeling especially big or energized during some of those times.

There were a few quieter weeks where I felt more like myself emotionally, at least as far as I could tell. But I still heard the lines talking, and I still thought the farm data had hidden warnings in it. I know that may sound odd… I’m just trying to answer it plainly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has ever had a major depressive episode, which would support schizoaffective disorder rather than schizophrenia or bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything you usually enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a depressive symptom—loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia) for at least two weeks—which is not included in the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. I mean, I’ve had times where I didn’t feel like doing much, sure, but “almost everything” for two weeks… I don’t know.

I still usually find some satisfaction in the farm or family things, even if it’s not the same. So I don’t want to give you the wrong answer—maybe not that I can clearly say.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have ever occurred exclusively during mood episodes or also independently, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Before these past eleven months, had you ever heard the voices or noticed those hidden warnings at a time when you were not feeling high or irritable?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The voices and coded warnings have been happening for about 11 months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timing/onset of the voices and hidden warnings relative to the past eleven months, which is most directly covered by the psychotic symptoms duration item.

patient.answer:
No… not that I can remember before this past year. The voices and those coded warnings, that all seems to have started around eleven months ago.

I might be missing something, but before then I don’t think I was noticing anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was any period of psychotic symptoms lasting at least one month without prominent mood symptoms, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Was there ever a full month when you were hearing the voices or noticing the hidden warnings while not feeling especially high or irritable?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There were several quieter weeks when I was not especially energized or grand, but I still heard the lines talking and still believed the farm data was carrying hidden warnings.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether psychotic symptoms—voices and hidden warnings—persisted for a sustained period while the patient was not in a high or irritable mood state.

patient.answer:
I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to overstate it, but there were several quieter weeks where I wasn’t feeling especially energized or grand or anything like that.

Even then, I was still hearing the lines talking, and I still believed the farm data had hidden warnings in it. So… if that counts as a full month, then yes, I think that did happen.

inference.note: Psychosis has persisted for at least 2 weeks outside mood episodes, ruling out F31.2. Presence of prominent manic episodes for the majority of the illness makes schizophrenia (F20.0) less likely and supports schizoaffective disorder, manic type.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for schizoaffective disorder, manic type: persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusional ideas about hidden warnings/poisoned or blessed rows) have been present for about 11 months, including at least 2 weeks when mood was relatively normal. He also has clear manic episodes with elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity, and severe functional impairment. Depressive episode criteria were not established, supporting the manic type rather than depressive type.
